note: Exact two reviews before v5 voice revision. Historical copy may contain unsupported claims; retained as rollback evidence, not a coaching template.

e89f68db-2b84-4433-b02c-2ffbf6cb43f4.headline: Won the fights. Finished the job.
e89f68db-2b84-4433-b02c-2ffbf6cb43f4.team: Most won fight sequences were followed by an objective or structure, and the final fight ran alongside the push into their base. The early Mini Prime exchange still deserves scrutiny: securing the objective did not erase the deaths.

focus.title: Name the next prize
focus.action: After the next won fight, call the nearest safely reachable objective or structure before anyone starts another chase.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Sparrow delivered the carry performance: team-leading damage and kills without a pile of deaths. Keep that balance. Make sustained damage with an escape option the standard next game; the scoreboard does not issue a license to donate his ass.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock combined strong farm with very few deaths. Keep the reliable income and survival. Review the death around Primal Fangtooth for a safer exit, then carry any clear correction forward without abandoning what worked.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Iggy & Scorch brought strong farm, substantial objective damage and excellent survival. Keep taking reachable farm and helping finish objectives. There is no prize for inflating hero damage by throwing away a productive game.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Lt. Belica supplied heavy ward placement and plenty of assists. Keep that involvement, but examine the early death to Revenant for a safer route or retreat. If a safer option was available, take that correction into the next match; strong support output does not cancel it.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Khaimera led objective damage and farmed above the recorded baseline. Keep the neutral pressure and reliable income. Before the next objective attempt, confirm an exit route so securing the prize does not require gambling the rest of the fight.

9.3.call: The kill sequence ended 1-3. Mini Prime was secured afterward; the objective take does not establish that the deaths were avoidable or worthwhile.

15.6.call: The kill sequence ended 3-0. Mini Prime was secured during it, an Outer Tower followed, and Fangtooth came later.

24.7.call: The final kill sequence ended 5-2 while enemy structures fell. Their Core fell shortly afterward.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Final inventory: Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher, Imperator.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Final inventory: Ashbringer, Claw Of Hermes, Sky Splitter.

768794a7-cdc9-4365-b767-4c70fefc3fb2.headline: The Core fell in a fight only two of five players showed up to.
768794a7-cdc9-4365-b767-4c70fefc3fb2.team: Towers finished 1-10, and the losing pattern was rotations more than fights: the offlane was credited in just 2 of 9 skirmishes despite 5 match assists, and the Core fell in a fight only two of five players joined, with the carry already dead and two more alive elsewhere. The squad won two fights outright but cashed neither, trading bodies for the enemy's Fangtooth, Primal Fangtooth and Orb Prime instead of getting anything back. One clean solo death in the mid lane directly preceded two inner towers and an inhibitor falling in the same stretch - one of two sequences that doomed the game, alongside the 30-31m stretch that cost two inhibitors and the Core.

focus.title: Show up when the numbers are already there
focus.action: When the team already has the bodies (5-vs-4 or better), every living player needs to be in the fight - the Inhibitor fell in a fight the offlane and midlane both sat out, and the Core fell in a fight only Steel and Gideon showed up for while the jungle and offlane stayed elsewhere.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Wukong's damage stayed well above the usual jungle rate, but the vision game cratered right after turning it around last game - zero wards this time against a comp that was three-fifths physical, and no armor for it either. Keep the damage; the vision fix from last game needs to actually stick. He was also alive and never made it to the fight that lost the Core - whatever the lane state, that's one to be in.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Revenant's six kills and three deaths look fine on the sheet, but the damage per minute was well below the usual carry rate, and none of his deaths were solo - all three came inside fights the team was already losing. Keep the low death count. The next step is turning kill involvement into real damage, especially in a lane he was never favored to win.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett survived clean after the opening two deaths and led the team in wards, but she was credited in just 2 of 9 skirmishes despite 5 match assists, including the fights that lost the Inhibitor and the Core. Objective damage has also been thin from this seat more than once this stretch. Keep the vision and the survival; the fix that matters most next game is being in the fight when the team already has the numbers.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Gideon's line was ordinary everywhere except the one moment that decided the midgame: caught alone by Crunch, a death that turned straight into two inner towers and an inhibitor falling right after. Keep the early kills on Yin and Mourn. The fix is narrow and clear - don't get caught alone in the mid lane that deep into a losing structure count. He also sat out the Inhibitor fight while the team had the numbers to win it.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel finished with zero kills and a death count that ran above the usual rate for the role, and the first one was the costly kind - caught alone by Murdock before ten minutes, feeding straight into the enemy's first Fangtooth. Keep the assists and the mitigation; a support can't afford that early solo death, full stop. The other three deaths came inside fights the team was already losing, so those aren't hers to fix.

25.call: A solo death in the mid lane at 25:00 opened the door - two inner towers and an inhibitor fell right after.

31.call: The Core fell at 31:00 in a fight only two of five joined, with the carry already dead and two more alive elsewhere.

10.7.call: The first Fangtooth went to them at 10:42 in a 5v5 fight where the offlane wasn't among the credited participants.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: No winning-core comparison exists for Wukong here either. He carried no armor against a three-fifths-physical comp, but the zero-ward game was the bigger issue this time.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Vanquisher, Terminus and Imperator match the full recommended core, plus one off-meta Demolisher. The low damage-per-minute isn't a build problem - the core was right.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Only three items finished all game: Mutilator landed, but Infernum and The Perforator from the recommended core never did. That reads as a slow, low-gold game more than a wrong build, and it doesn't explain the fights she missed.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings match the full recommended core with nothing off-meta mixed in. The build wasn't the issue this game - the solo death was.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xenia, Dynamo and Stonewall cover two of the three recommended core items, missing only Gaia Greaves, plus one off-meta Tainted Guard. Nothing here explains the early solo death or the scoreless game.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Steel's Eternal contribution isn't modeled in this review, so no claim follows about Krix's effectiveness here.
